issuing_body: United States District Court, District of Minnesota
title: Opinion and Order, State of Minnesota et al. v. Oz et al., No. 0:26-cv-01701, ECF 43
court: United States District Court, District of Minnesota
supports: Minnesota challenged the CMS February 25, 2026 Medicaid deferral in federal court and sought temporary and preliminary injunctive relief.
On April 6, 2026, Judge Eric C. Tostrud denied Minnesota's motion for a temporary restraining order and expedited preliminary injunction.
The order treats the CMS deferral as an ongoing administrative process rather than a final agency determination that the deferred claims are disallowed.

The court states that CMS had identified approximately $164.2 million in federal financial participation associated with questionable variances and approximately $79.6 million associated with claims from providers CMS identified as high-risk for fraud or aberrant billing practices, and had requested supporting documentation or decreasing adjustments.

The court expressly notes that the deferral notice did not conclude that the questioned claims would ultimately be disallowed and that a deferral may later result in disallowance of all, part, or none of the questioned amount depending on the administrative process.
The court also records that CMS approved Minnesota's January 30 revised corrective action plan on March 19, 2026, but treated the CAP approval and the Medicaid-claim deferral as distinct processes.
important_qualifications: Denial of preliminary relief was not a merits judgment that the deferred Medicaid claims were fraudulent or unallowable.
The ruling did not finally resolve the amount of federal funding Minnesota will receive or lose.
The court's factual recitation of CMS's questioned-claim categories describes the administrative record; it does not convert those claims into adjudicated fraud loss.
